title: An Aadhaar number written in Hindi digits or with dots is kept in the member notes after an import
what: The import promises to leave Aadhaar and PAN numbers out. It only finds an Aadhaar written in plain 0-9 digits with spaces or dashes. The same number written in Hindi (or another Indian) digits, or as 2345.6789.0123, is saved into the member's notes or extra details. The AI step that sees sample rows already hides these forms, so the two checks disagree.
expected: Every Aadhaar the AI step would hide is also cut out of what the import saves: any Indian digits, and dots or slashes between the groups.
how_often: rare: a register that writes Aadhaar in Hindi digits or with dots
fix_line: Turn every Indian digit into 0-9 and treat dots and slashes as separators before looking for an Aadhaar

title: The import reads mobiles in Hindi digits, but not dates or fees, so such a row is refused
what: A sheet whose mobiles are in Hindi digits imports fine, but a joining date like 15/08/2026 written in Hindi digits is "not a date we can read" and the whole row is refused. Birthdays, plan dates and fees in Hindi digits are dropped with a warning. A mobile written with +91 in Hindi digits is refused too. The trainer's body measurement boxes and the reminder days box also refuse Hindi keyboard digits.
expected: Every number the import and these boxes read takes the same digits the mobile boxes already take.
how_often: rare: registers kept in Hindi digits, or a Hindi keyboard
fix_line: Turn Indian digits into 0-9 once, before any date, amount or number is read
